'''Houda-Imane Faraoun''', also spelled  '''Feraoun''', is an Algerian [[physicist]] and [[materials scientist]] who was appointed Minister of Post, Information Technology & Communication in the government of Algerian Prime Minister [[Abdelmalek Sellal]] on 1 May 2015.<ref name="auto2">{{cite web |url=http://www.forbesmiddleeast.com/en/lists/people/pname/iman-houda-fearoun/pid/86607/ |title=Iman Houda Fearoun – &#124; Forbes Middle East |accessdate=15 February 2016 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303170720/http://www.forbesmiddleeast.com/en/lists/people/pname/iman-houda-fearoun/pid/86607/ |archivedate=3 March 2016 }}</ref> She is also a professor of physics at the [[University of Tlemcen]], a post she has held in various capacities since 2006.<ref name="auto">{{cite web |url=http://www.tsa-algerie.com/20150903/biographie-de-decideur-houda-imane-faraoun/ |title=Biographie de décideur : Houda Imane Faraoun &#124; Info & Actualités depuis 2007 |accessdate=15 February 2016 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303200019/http://www.tsa-algerie.com/20150903/biographie-de-decideur-houda-imane-faraoun/ |archivedate=3 March 2016 }}</ref> She holds a PhD in [[physics]] from the [[University Djillali Liabès of Sidi Bel Abbès]] and a PhD in mechanical engineering from the [[University of Technology of Belfort-Montbéliard]].<ref name="auto1">{{cite web | title=Biographie de la Ministre|publisher=Ministère de la poste et des technologies de l'information et de la communication | website=mptic.dz | date=14 May 2015 | url=http://www.mptic.dz/fr/?-Curriculum-vitae-du-Ministre- | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160215212049/http://www.mptic.dz/fr/?-Curriculum-vitae-du-Ministre- | archive-date=15 February 2016 | url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2021 she was sentenced to prison for embezzlement.

==Early life==
Faraoun was born in Sidi Bel Abbès, Algeria on 16 June 1979.<ref name="auto1"/> She received her baccalaureate at the age of 16. In 1999, at the age of 20, she received a degree (DES) in Physics from the University of Sidi Bel Abbès and began her studies for a doctorate in [[Solid-state Physics]] at the same institution.<ref name="auto"/> A determined student, she concurrently pursued a doctorate at the [[University of Technology of Belfort-Montbéliard]] in Mechanical Engineering. In 2005, she received PhDs from both universities.<ref name="auto1"/>

==Career==
In 2006, Faraoun was named an instructor and researcher at the [[University of Tlemcen]], a city in western Algeria. From 2010 to 2011, she served as the head of the university's [[Condensed Matter Physics]] department.<ref name="auto1"/> While still teaching, Faraoun served as the director general of Algeria's Agency for Thematic Research, Science & Technology (ATRST) from 2012 to 2015. Her research at the University of Tlemcen focuses on [[materials science]] and [[computational physics]]. Over the course of her career, she has published more than forty articles in international scientific journals.<ref name="auto1"/> Her most recent scientific publication, "Determination of Mechanical Properties of Porous Silicon with Image Analysis and Finite Element," was presented at the 8th International Conference on Material Sciences in December 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/275544989|title=Determination of Mechanical Properties of Porous Silicon with Image Analysis and Finite Element (PDF Download Available)|website=ResearchGate|access-date=16 November 2017}}</ref>

Faraoun was appointed as Minister of Post, Information Technology & Communication by Prime Minister [[Abdelmalek Sellal]] on 1 May 2015 during a larger cabinet re-shuffling.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.jeuneafrique.com/231825/politique/remaniement-en-alg-rie-int-rieur-nergie-et-finances-changent-de-mains/|title=Remaniement en Algérie: Intérieur, Énergie et Finances changent de mains – JeuneAfrique.com|date=14 May 2015|work=JeuneAfrique.com|access-date=16 November 2017|language=fr-FR}}</ref> She is the youngest minister in the current Algerian cabinet, and one of the youngest women ministers in the country's history.<ref name="auto"/> Along with [[Aïcha Tagabou]] and [[Mounia Meslem]], she is one of only three women in the current Algerian cabinet.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.tsa-algerie.com/20150514/nouveau-gouvernemen-la-liste-complete/ |title=Nouveau gouvernement: La liste complète &#124; Info & Actualités depuis 2007 |access-date=15 February 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160311001645/http://www.tsa-algerie.com/20150514/nouveau-gouvernemen-la-liste-complete/ |archive-date=11 March 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2015, [[Forbes]] named Faraoun No. 9 on its list of the Ten Most Powerful Arab Women in Government.<ref name="auto2"/> On 24 December 2020 she and former Minister of Industry [[Djamila Tamazirt]] appeared before the investigating judge at the fourth chamber of the specialized criminal pole at the tribunal of Sidi M'hamed. She was sentenced to three years in prison and a fine of one million dinars for "squandering public funds" and "granting of undue privileges and abuse of office" related to two contracts for optical fiber. The sentence was confirmed on 9 February 2022.<ref name=reporters>{{Cite news |title=Justice: L'ex-ministre Houda Imane Faraoun condamnée en appel à 3 ans de prison ferme |trans-title=Courts: Ex-minister Houda Imane Faraoun sentenced on appeal to 3 years in prison |author=<!--not stated--> |work=REPORTERS ALGERIE |date=10 February 2022 |url= https://www.reporters.dz/justice-lex-ministre-houda-imane-faraoun-condamnee-en-appel-a-3-ans-de-prison-ferme/ |language=fr}}</ref>
